Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI) stock is up 35% year to date, a strong run that still lands well behind Texas Instruments. Analog Devices rode the same industrial and communications tailwind, yet Texas Instruments converted that demand into more revenue and did so with a manufacturing footprint already sized for the recovery.
Additionally, Microchip Technology (NASDAQ:MCHP) stock is up 15% year to date, the widest gap of the three. The through-line for Texas Instruments is that in analog, the constraint during an upturn is usually the ability to supply rather than the ability to sell. Texas Instruments guided third-quarter revenue to $5.65 billion to $6.15 billion and EPS to $2.23 to $2.57, a range that would extend the sequential and year-over-year growth pattern. The bull case for Texas Instruments rests on Ilan's view that the cycle is early and unusually broad, with industrial, data center and automotive contributing at once, and with pricing rising in a business where it normally erodes.
TXN Price Scenario — 24/7 Wall St.
The bear case for Texas Instruments is that an analog upcycle remains a cycle, and a stock that's added more than half its value in under a year has already priced a fair stretch of it. Trailing its own semiconductor fund is both why Texas Instruments reads as an overlooked story (the kind we cataloged in a free report on the winners most investors walked past) and why the market may prefer the chips that train models to the ones powering the racks around them.
Investors weighing fresh exposure to Texas Instruments may want to keep an eye on whether the third-quarter pricing actions hold, and size their positions with that duality in mind. The pending Silicon Labs transaction, which Texas Instruments still expects to close in the first half of 2027, gives it another lever if the broad cycle extends into next year.

TXN Surges 67% Over the Past Year: Is the Stock Still Worth Buying?
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 6:29 AM PDT 5 min read
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN has been one of the standout performers in the semiconductor industry over the past year. The stock has surged 66.6%, easily beating the broader Zacks Semiconductor – General industry, which advanced 34.6%.
TXN has also outperformed several major semiconductor names, including Broadcom Inc. AVGO, QUALCOMM Incorporated QCOM and NVIDIA Corporation NVDA. Over the past year, shares of Broadcom, QUALCOMM and NVIDIA have risen 7.8%, 9.3% and 29.6%, respectively.
After such a strong rally, investors may wonder whether it is too late to buy Texas Instruments. In our view, the stock still has upside potential. Its valuation is high, but improving earnings, growing AI-related demand, strong cash generation and major manufacturing investments provide a solid foundation for further growth.
Texas Instruments One-year Price Return Performance
Texas Instruments' Strong Results Keep the Bull Case Alive
TXN's recent results show that the business is gaining momentum. Second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 23% year over year to $5.46 billion, while non-GAAP earnings rose 52% to $2.14 per share.
The guidance is equally encouraging. Texas Instruments expects third-quarter revenues of $5.65-$6.15 billion, with the midpoint representing about 25% year-over-year growth. The midpoint of its earnings per share guidance is $2.40, implying growth of nearly 62%. The guidance reflects healthy demand across several markets, particularly those tied to AI infrastructure.
Wall Street shares the same optimism. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for continued revenue and earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027, reinforcing confidence that the company's growth story is far from over.
Texas Instruments Sales and EPS Growth Forecast
AI Is Becoming a Bigger Opportunity for Texas Instruments
Texas Instruments is not an AI accelerator company like NVIDIA or AMD, but it is becoming an important beneficiary of the AI boom. TXN makes analog and embedded chips that help manage power, process signals and control equipment used in data centers and industrial systems. As AI data centers become more powerful, they require more electricity and increasingly sophisticated power-management systems.
Instead of competing in the crowded AI processor market, the company is benefiting from the broader AI infrastructure buildout. This positions Texas Instruments to capture AI spending regardless of which GPU (graphics processing unit) maker ultimately dominates the data center market.
The numbers already reflect this trend. Texas Instruments' data center business reached an annual revenue run rate of approximately $1.2 billion in 2025, growing more than 50% year over year. During the second quarter of 2026, data center revenues doubled from the prior-year quarter and increased 20% sequentially.
Such strong growth suggests AI infrastructure could become an increasingly important revenue driver over the coming years. If AI data center investment remains strong, TXN's exposure could expand without requiring the company to compete directly in the highly competitive accelerator market.
Manufacturing Expansion Could Add to TXN's Advantage
Texas Instruments is also investing heavily to bring more manufacturing in-house. Unlike many semiconductor companies that depend heavily on third-party foundries, TXN plans to produce more than 95% of its wafers internally by 2030.
While this strategy requires substantial capital spending, it could provide greater control over supply and improve cost efficiency. This could become an important competitive advantage as semiconductor demand grows.
Government support should also help reduce the financial burden. Texas Instruments expects to receive up to $1.6 billion in direct CHIPS Act grants and another $6-$8 billion from the U.S. Treasury Department's Investment Tax Credit. Including both, total lifetime benefits are estimated between $7.5 billion and $9.5 billion. These incentives should reduce expansion costs and boost profitability over the long run.
TXN's Strong Cash Flow Supports More Investment and Returns
Texas Instruments' cash generation further strengthens its ability to invest while returning capital to shareholders. Over the past 12 months, the company generated $8.67 billion in operating cash flow and $6.53 billion in free cash flow. It ended the second quarter with $7 billion in cash and short-term investments.
The company also continues to reward investors. During the first half of 2026, TXN returned nearly $1.45 billion through dividends and share repurchases. Over the past year, total shareholder returns approached $6 billion.
The strong cash position allows Texas Instruments to invest aggressively in manufacturing expansion while continuing to reward shareholders.
Texas Instruments' Premium Valuation May Be Justified
Texas Instruments is not a bargain stock. It currently carries a Value Score of D, reflecting its premium valuation. TXN currently trades at a forward 12-month P/E ratio of 30.99, well above the industry average of 19.04.
Texas Instruments Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio
Compared with other semiconductor leaders, Texas Instruments also trades at a higher earnings multiple than Broadcom, QUALCOMM and NVIDIA. At present, Broadcom, QUALCOMM and NVIDIA are trading at P/E multiples of 19.56, 17.97 and 17.67, respectively.
However, premium valuations are often justified when a company consistently delivers earnings growth, generates strong cash flow and maintains durable competitive advantages.
Texas Instruments fits that profile. The company continues to benefit from expanding AI infrastructure spending, generates substantial free cash flow, maintains a healthy balance sheet and has a long track record of rewarding shareholders through dividends and share buybacks. Those strengths make its premium valuation easier to justify.
Final Verdict: TXN Stock Is Still Worth Buying
Texas Instruments has already delivered an impressive 66.6% gain over the past year, but the investment story is not over.
While the stock is not inexpensive, the underlying business remains strong enough to support the premium. The company's accelerating earnings, strong data center growth, expanding AI exposure and manufacturing investments point to further long-term opportunities. Its strong cash generation also gives it flexibility to invest while continuing to reward shareholders.

As the artificial intelligence boom matures, choosing between high-growth processors and steady analog chips requires a careful look at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +2.80%) and Texas Instruments (TXN +0.79%) as potential long-term investments.
Advanced Micro Devices focuses on high-performance computing for data centers and gaming, while Texas Instruments dominates the analog world with chips for industrial and automotive uses. While both operate in the same broad category, their business models and growth profiles offer very different opportunities for retail investors today.
Advanced Micro Devices designs processors and graphics chips for everything from laptops to massive data centers. Key partnerships include a strategic agreement with OpenAI to deploy advanced graphics units, alongside long-term deals with Sony (SONY +1.32%) and Microsoft (MSFT +0.78%) for gaming hardware. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business since a few large buyers drive much of the volume.
In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $34.6 billion, an increase of 34% over the prior year. Net income was roughly $4.3 billion, and AMD reported a net margin of approximately 12.5% for the year. This upward trend highlights the strong demand for the company's newest products among semiconductor stocks.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1, indicating that AMD relies very little on borrowed money. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to pay short-term debts with current assets, is roughly 2.9. Free cash flow reached nearly $6.7 billion, though note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 21.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
Texas Instruments offers a massive catalog of more than 80,000 products, focusing on analog and embedded processing. The company serves over 100,000 customers globally, primarily in the industrial and automotive markets. Because the customer base is highly diverse, with roughly half of total revenue generated by customers outside of its largest 50, the company does not rely heavily on any single buyer.
In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $17.7 billion, up 13% compared to the previous year. Net income was $5 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 28%. In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, Texas Instruments highlighted its focus on making electronics more affordable through its manufacturing scale.
Based on the December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is close to 0.9. The current ratio is approximately 4.4, suggesting the company maintains a strong cushion for its immediate financial obligations. Free cash flow for the year was nearly $2.6 billion, providing capital to support its long-term manufacturing expansion and return value to shareholders.
Advanced Micro Devices faces intense competition from Intel (INTC -3.18%) and Nvidia (NVDA +0.14%), especially following strategic partnerships between those rivals. Geopolitical risks are also present, as U.S. export controls on advanced chips to China have caused inventory charges. Additionally, the company relies heavily on TSMC (TSM -0.72%) for manufacturing and must navigate the integration of recent acquisitions like ZT Systems.
Texas Instruments must manage the cyclical nature of the chip industry, which often sees volatile demand. Because the company owns its manufacturing plants, it faces high fixed costs that are difficult to reduce during market downturns. Significant revenue comes from customers in China, making it vulnerable to trade barriers. TI is also currently in the middle of acquiring Silicon Laboratories (SLAB -0.08%).
Advanced Micro Devices trades at a significantly higher premium than Texas Instruments when comparing the forward P/E and P/S ratio metrics.
MetricAdvanced Micro DevicesTexas Instruments
Valuation metrics sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Presumably, investors are paying a premium for AMD because of its strong revenue growth (Texas Instruments' growth didn't come close to AMD's last fiscal year). That said, I am more interested in each company's net margin. Using fiscal 2025 figures, TI's margin pretty handily tops AMD's full-year results. And while both companies have seen profits expand by a few percentage points over the trailing 12 months, that profitability gap has continued into this fiscal year.
As far as their actual business models, I do think AMD's fabless approach is more attractive, because it gives the company more flexibility. Texas Instruments, conversely, has to deal with the high fixed costs of owning and running its manufacturing plants.
AMD stock has absolutely exploded over the past 10 years, while Texas Instruments shares have modestly outperformed the S&P 500 over that same time frame. Past performance is no indication of future results, but it's worth taking into consideration.
All told, I like Texas Instruments better here because it appeals to the conservative side of me: It’s not crazy expensive, it has stronger profitability, and it pays a dividend yielding just over 2.1%.

Can TXN's 300mm Fab Expansion Strategy Further Boost Margins?

Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN is nearing the payoff phase of its long-term 300mm manufacturing investment, which could provide a structural lift to margins as factory utilization improves. The company claims 300mm production costs about 40% less per chip than production on 200mm wafers. This will give TXN a meaningful cost advantage as more output shifts to larger wafers. Texas Instruments' six-year elevated capital expenditure cycle for its 300mm wafer fabs will conclude in 2026.
The strategy is already supporting financial performance. In the second quarter of 2026, Texas Instruments reported $5.46 billion in revenues, up 23% year over year, while gross profit increased 30% to $3.35 billion. Gross margin reached 61.4%, up 350 basis points from 57.9% in the year-ago quarter.
Management also credited the benefits of 300mm production as a factor supporting its strong cash generation. The company generated free cash flow of $2.74 billion in the second quarter, up from $1.33 billion in the year-ago quarter. Trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $6.53 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 271% from $1.76 billion in the year-ago period.
Higher factory utilization could provide another margin boost. As much of TXN's manufacturing cost is fixed, stronger production spreads those costs over more chips. Management expects to equip its existing clean-room capacity based on customer demand, allowing it to increase output without immediately taking on the full cost of building new facilities.
TXN is entering this phase with lower capital spending requirements. The company expects 2026 capital expenditures of $2-$3 billion, down from $4.55 billion in 2025.
As 300mm capacity ramps up and utilization rises, TXN could benefit from lower unit costs, better operating leverage and stronger free cash flow. However, the pace of margin expansion will depend on demand and how quickly the new facilities reach efficient utilization.
What TXN's Rivals Are Doing to Improve Manufacturing Margins
Texas Instruments' major competitors, Analog Devices, Inc. ADI and ON Semiconductor Corporation ON, have different strategies to improve manufacturing margins.
Analog Devices is enhancing its manufacturing margins by executing a multi-pronged strategy centered around a hybrid manufacturing model, strategic price increases and optimized asset utilization. With the hybrid manufacturing model, ADI can swiftly pivot production based on demand without incurring heavy capital expenditures. The strategy helps the company protect margins from the fixed-cost burdens of overbuilding factories and supports high free cash flow conversion.
In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Analog Devices' revenues increased 40% year-over-year to $4.02 billion, while non-GAAP gross profit jumped 46% to $2.92 billion. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 72.5%, up 330 basis points from 69.2% in the year-ago quarter. Its trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $4.94 billion in the third quarter, up 34% from $3.68 billion in the year-ago period.
ON Semiconductor is taking a more direct approach to manufacturing efficiency through its Fab Right strategy. The company is consolidating its manufacturing footprint and expanding 300mm capacity while exiting less efficient facilities. ON claims that its streamlined fabrication footprint could operate at about 17% lower cost at full utilization.
ON Semiconductor's non-GAAP gross margin improved 80 basis points sequentially to 39.3% in second-quarter 2026, while manufacturing utilization rose to 83% from 77%. Management expects sequential gross margin expansion through 2026 and guided third-quarter non-GAAP gross margin to 40%-42% on revenues of $1.65-$1.75 billion. The planned Mountain Top and Philippines facility divestitures are expected to generate about $35 million of annualized savings, with benefits beginning in 2027 and fully realized in 2028. Management forecasts these actions represent roughly 50 basis points of the planned 200 basis points of gross margin improvement from Fab Right initiatives.

Zephyr Project Expands Semiconductor Industry Support as Texas Instruments and Infineon Technologies Upgrade to Platinum Membership

Texas Instruments and Infineon Technologies have upgraded to Platinum membership in the Zephyr Project, deepening their investment in the open source RTOS and its developer community.
These increased commitments provide additional resources for Zephyr's technical development, infrastructure and community programs.
The announcement coincides with the Zephyr Developer Summit (Oct. 7-9) and Zephyr Maintainers Forum (Oct. 6) in Prague, where the community marks Zephyr's 10th anniversary with more than 40 technical sessions, over 45 speakers and the first-ever Zephyr Community Awards.
PRAGUE, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zephyr Developer Summit – The Zephyr® Project, an open source project at the Linux Foundation building a secure, connected and flexible real-time operating system (RTOS) for resource-constrained devices, today announced that Texas Instruments (TI) and Infineon Technologies have upgraded to Platinum membership. Announced ahead of the Zephyr Developer Summit, co-located with Open Source Summit Europe, the expanded commitments from two leading semiconductor companies reinforce growing industry investment in Zephyr as a vendor-neutral, open source foundation for embedded development.
TI and Infineon bring longstanding technical relationships with the Zephyr community. TI has contributed to the project since its inception in 2016, providing software and board support while integrating Zephyr across its embedded portfolio. Infineon is also an active contributor and supports Zephyr across multiple embedded platforms. The move to Platinum membership will provide additional resources for the project's technical development, infrastructure and community programs.
"Ten years ago, Zephyr set out to give the embedded industry a common open source RTOS that companies could build on together," said Kate Stewart, Vice President of Dependable Embedded Systems at the Linux Foundation. "Seeing two major semiconductor companies that have contributed to Zephyr for years increase their participation is a strong sign of how far that model has come. This support gives the community more resources and makes Zephyr available to more developers building embedded products."
Since its launch, Zephyr has grown into a global ecosystem spanning a broad range of architectures, boards and embedded applications. As open source plays a growing role in embedded development, Zephyr provides a common platform where semiconductor companies, developers and product manufacturers can collaborate on shared technology. The increased engagement from TI and Infineon will help Zephyr advance its technology, hardware ecosystem and developer community as it enters its second decade.
"As a platinum-level member, Infineon is expanding its investment in the Zephyr community to help developers bring connected, resource-constrained devices to market more efficiently," said Clark Jarvis, Zephyr Governing Board Representative at Infineon. "Building on a decade of Zephyr innovation, we are committed to enabling greater software reuse and portability across our microcontroller (MCU), automotive MCU, and connectivity portfolios. This deeper engagement reflects our ambition to deliver an even better developer experience, strengthen security, and broaden hardware support throughout the Zephyr ecosystem."
"TI is committed to breaking down the barriers between hardware and software through continuous innovation. The Zephyr Project is a cornerstone of that effort," said Marian Kost, vice president and general manager of Wireless Connectivity at TI. "We are continuing our investment in open-source software and the developer community. TI wants to ensure that everyone – from a hobbyist to an engineer – can accelerate their path from concept to commercial product."
The upgraded memberships come as the Zephyr community gathers in Prague at Open Source Summit Europe to continue celebrating the project's tenth anniversary. The week opens with the Zephyr Maintainers Forum on Oct. 6, a working session where maintainers, Technical Steering Committee members and subsystem owners set the project's technical direction on release planning, security and safety support, and cross-subsystem coordination. It is followed by the Zephyr Developer Summit on Oct. 7-9, featuring more than 40 technical sessions from over 45 speakers across functional safety, security and CRA readiness, connectivity, developer tooling and testing, and real-world use cases in automotive, space and industrial applications. The summit also hosts the Zephyr Community Awards on Oct. 7, recognizing standout contributors from across the ecosystem for their work and support over the last decade.
Check out the complete Zephyr Developer Summit schedule or to learn more about the Zephyr Project and how to participate, visit zephyrproject.org.
The Zephyr® Project is an open source, scalable real-time operating system (RTOS) supporting multiple hardware architectures. To learn more, please visit www.zephyrproject.org.
The Linux Foundation is the world's leading home for collaboration on open source software, hardware, standards, and data. Linux Foundation projects, including Linux, Kubernetes, Model Context Protocol (MCP), OpenChain, OpenSearch, OpenSSF, OpenStack, PyTorch, Ray, RISC-V, SPDX and Zephyr, provide the foundation for global infrastructure. The Linux Foundation is focused on leveraging best practices and addressing the needs of contributors, users, and solution providers to create sustainable models for open collaboration. Management Set A Higher Bar For Texas Instruments; Does The Chart Agree?
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 10:09 AM PDT 4 min read
Texas Instruments (TXN) forecast higher third-quarter sales and earnings on July 22, 2026, and the stock has since risen, though by less than the S&P 500. A forecast is only management's word until buyers act on it, so the share price is worth checking before you take the guide at face value. Have buyers of Texas Instruments stock been backing that forecast?
Does Texas Instruments' Chart Back The Forecast?
Only partly. Texas Instruments stock is in an uptrend on its own chart, but it has trailed the market since the forecast came out.
The shares closed at $294.90 on October 5, 2026. That is above $270.73, their average closing price over the last 50 trading days. That average is, in turn, above $247.77, the average close over the last 200 trading days. A stock above both averages, with the shorter one on top, is in an uptrend.
The return since the release is weaker. Texas Instruments gave the quarter's results and the forecast in one release, so buyers were reacting to both. The stock fell 2.2% over the two sessions around it, while the S&P 500 fell 1.3%. From the July 22 close immediately following the post-market release through October 5, the stock is up 0.8%, compared to a 3.5% gain for the S&P 500. So the stock is above both averages today, but Texas Instruments has not beaten the market since management spoke.
Texas Instruments Forecast Higher Sales And Earnings
Management guided to third-quarter 2026 revenue of $5.65 billion to $6.15 billion. That quarter has since ended, and its results are still to come. The middle of that range, $5.9 billion, compares with the $5.5 billion the company reported for the second quarter. The second quarter had itself beaten the plan: revenue grew 23% from a year earlier and came in above management's own range.
Management credited that result to continued growth in its industrial and data center markets and faster growth in automotive. Data center revenue doubled from a year earlier. For the third quarter, management said the vast majority of the expected growth is more units sold, with almost nothing coming from price.
Management forecast higher earnings too. It guided to $2.23 to $2.57 a share for the third quarter, against the $2.14 it reported for the second.
What Could Push Texas Instruments Stock Higher?
Higher prices and growth in Texas Instruments' industrial market could, if the third- and fourth-quarter results bear out what management said on the July call. Texas Instruments has started increasing prices. Management said in July that almost none of the effect was in its third-quarter forecast, and that it expected the increases to continue into the fourth quarter.
The industrial market is the other place to look. Management said its industrial market is still below its 2022 peak, and it sees room to grow there. But you are paying 44.4 times trailing twelve-month earnings for the stock, compared to a trailing P/E of 21.5 for the S&P 500.
So management's forecast and the uptrend agree today, and the lag behind the market is the weak spot. Third-quarter revenue above the top of management's range would show demand still running ahead of what the company planned for. Fourth-quarter guidance with a visible lift from price would show the increases are holding. A close below the average of the last 50 trading days would be the first sign that buyers have stopped backing the forecast.

TXN Surges 67% Over the Past Year: Is the Stock Still Worth Buying?
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 6:29 AM PDT 5 min read
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN has been one of the standout performers in the semiconductor industry over the past year. The stock has surged 66.6%, easily beating the broader Zacks Semiconductor – General industry, which advanced 34.6%.
TXN has also outperformed several major semiconductor names, including Broadcom Inc. AVGO, QUALCOMM Incorporated QCOM and NVIDIA Corporation NVDA. Over the past year, shares of Broadcom, QUALCOMM and NVIDIA have risen 7.8%, 9.3% and 29.6%, respectively.
After such a strong rally, investors may wonder whether it is too late to buy Texas Instruments. In our view, the stock still has upside potential. Its valuation is high, but improving earnings, growing AI-related demand, strong cash generation and major manufacturing investments provide a solid foundation for further growth.
Texas Instruments One-year Price Return Performance
Texas Instruments' Strong Results Keep the Bull Case Alive
TXN's recent results show that the business is gaining momentum. Second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 23% year over year to $5.46 billion, while non-GAAP earnings rose 52% to $2.14 per share.
The guidance is equally encouraging. Texas Instruments expects third-quarter revenues of $5.65-$6.15 billion, with the midpoint representing about 25% year-over-year growth. The midpoint of its earnings per share guidance is $2.40, implying growth of nearly 62%. The guidance reflects healthy demand across several markets, particularly those tied to AI infrastructure.
Wall Street shares the same optimism. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for continued revenue and earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027, reinforcing confidence that the company's growth story is far from over.
Texas Instruments Sales and EPS Growth Forecast
AI Is Becoming a Bigger Opportunity for Texas Instruments
Texas Instruments is not an AI accelerator company like NVIDIA or AMD, but it is becoming an important beneficiary of the AI boom. TXN makes analog and embedded chips that help manage power, process signals and control equipment used in data centers and industrial systems. As AI data centers become more powerful, they require more electricity and increasingly sophisticated power-management systems.
Instead of competing in the crowded AI processor market, the company is benefiting from the broader AI infrastructure buildout. This positions Texas Instruments to capture AI spending regardless of which GPU (graphics processing unit) maker ultimately dominates the data center market.
The numbers already reflect this trend. Texas Instruments' data center business reached an annual revenue run rate of approximately $1.2 billion in 2025, growing more than 50% year over year. During the second quarter of 2026, data center revenues doubled from the prior-year quarter and increased 20% sequentially.
Such strong growth suggests AI infrastructure could become an increasingly important revenue driver over the coming years. If AI data center investment remains strong, TXN's exposure could expand without requiring the company to compete directly in the highly competitive accelerator market.
Manufacturing Expansion Could Add to TXN's Advantage
Texas Instruments is also investing heavily to bring more manufacturing in-house. Unlike many semiconductor companies that depend heavily on third-party foundries, TXN plans to produce more than 95% of its wafers internally by 2030.
While this strategy requires substantial capital spending, it could provide greater control over supply and improve cost efficiency. This could become an important competitive advantage as semiconductor demand grows.
Government support should also help reduce the financial burden. Texas Instruments expects to receive up to $1.6 billion in direct CHIPS Act grants and another $6-$8 billion from the U.S. Treasury Department's Investment Tax Credit. Including both, total lifetime benefits are estimated between $7.5 billion and $9.5 billion. These incentives should reduce expansion costs and boost profitability over the long run.
TXN's Strong Cash Flow Supports More Investment and Returns
Texas Instruments' cash generation further strengthens its ability to invest while returning capital to shareholders. Over the past 12 months, the company generated $8.67 billion in operating cash flow and $6.53 billion in free cash flow. It ended the second quarter with $7 billion in cash and short-term investments.
The company also continues to reward investors. During the first half of 2026, TXN returned nearly $1.45 billion through dividends and share repurchases. Over the past year, total shareholder returns approached $6 billion.
The strong cash position allows Texas Instruments to invest aggressively in manufacturing expansion while continuing to reward shareholders.
Texas Instruments' Premium Valuation May Be Justified
Texas Instruments is not a bargain stock. It currently carries a Value Score of D, reflecting its premium valuation. TXN currently trades at a forward 12-month P/E ratio of 30.99, well above the industry average of 19.04.
Texas Instruments Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

However, premium valuations are often justified when a company consistently delivers earnings growth, generates strong cash flow and maintains durable competitive advantages.
Texas Instruments fits that profile. The company continues to benefit from expanding AI infrastructure spending, generates substantial free cash flow, maintains a healthy balance sheet and has a long track record of rewarding shareholders through dividends and share buybacks. Those strengths make its premium valuation easier to justify.
Final Verdict: TXN Stock Is Still Worth Buying
Texas Instruments has already delivered an impressive 66.6% gain over the past year, but the investment story is not over.
While the stock is not inexpensive, the underlying business remains strong enough to support the premium. The company's accelerating earnings, strong data center growth, expanding AI exposure and manufacturing investments point to further long-term opportunities. Its strong cash generation also gives it flexibility to invest while continuing to reward shareholders.

As the artificial intelligence boom matures, choosing between high-growth processors and steady analog chips requires a careful look at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +2.80%) and Texas Instruments (TXN +0.79%) as potential long-term investments.
Advanced Micro Devices focuses on high-performance computing for data centers and gaming, while Texas Instruments dominates the analog world with chips for industrial and automotive uses. While both operate in the same broad category, their business models and growth profiles offer very different opportunities for retail investors today.
Advanced Micro Devices designs processors and graphics chips for everything from laptops to massive data centers. Key partnerships include a strategic agreement with OpenAI to deploy advanced graphics units, alongside long-term deals with Sony (SONY +1.32%) and Microsoft (MSFT +0.78%) for gaming hardware. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business since a few large buyers drive much of the volume.
In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $34.6 billion, an increase of 34% over the prior year. Net income was roughly $4.3 billion, and AMD reported a net margin of approximately 12.5% for the year. This upward trend highlights the strong demand for the company's newest products among semiconductor stocks.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1, indicating that AMD relies very little on borrowed money. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to pay short-term debts with current assets, is roughly 2.9. Free cash flow reached nearly $6.7 billion, though note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 21.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
Texas Instruments offers a massive catalog of more than 80,000 products, focusing on analog and embedded processing. The company serves over 100,000 customers globally, primarily in the industrial and automotive markets. Because the customer base is highly diverse, with roughly half of total revenue generated by customers outside of its largest 50, the company does not rely heavily on any single buyer.
In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $17.7 billion, up 13% compared to the previous year. Net income was $5 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 28%. In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, Texas Instruments highlighted its focus on making electronics more affordable through its manufacturing scale.
Based on the December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is close to 0.9. The current ratio is approximately 4.4, suggesting the company maintains a strong cushion for its immediate financial obligations. Free cash flow for the year was nearly $2.6 billion, providing capital to support its long-term manufacturing expansion and return value to shareholders.
Advanced Micro Devices faces intense competition from Intel (INTC -3.18%) and Nvidia (NVDA +0.14%), especially following strategic partnerships between those rivals. Geopolitical risks are also present, as U.S. export controls on advanced chips to China have caused inventory charges. Additionally, the company relies heavily on TSMC (TSM -0.72%) for manufacturing and must navigate the integration of recent acquisitions like ZT Systems.
Texas Instruments must manage the cyclical nature of the chip industry, which often sees volatile demand. Because the company owns its manufacturing plants, it faces high fixed costs that are difficult to reduce during market downturns. Significant revenue comes from customers in China, making it vulnerable to trade barriers. TI is also currently in the middle of acquiring Silicon Laboratories (SLAB -0.08%).

Presumably, investors are paying a premium for AMD because of its strong revenue growth (Texas Instruments' growth didn't come close to AMD's last fiscal year). As far as their actual business models, I do think AMD's fabless approach is more attractive, because it gives the company more flexibility. Texas Instruments, conversely, has to deal with the high fixed costs of owning and running its manufacturing plants.
AMD stock has absolutely exploded over the past 10 years, while Texas Instruments shares have modestly outperformed the S&P 500 over that same time frame. Past performance is no indication of future results, but it's worth taking into consideration.

Can TXN's 300mm Fab Expansion Strategy Further Boost Margins?
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 5:39 AM PDT 4 min read
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN is nearing the payoff phase of its long-term 300mm manufacturing investment, which could provide a structural lift to margins as factory utilization improves. The company claims 300mm production costs about 40% less per chip than production on 200mm wafers. This will give TXN a meaningful cost advantage as more output shifts to larger wafers. Texas Instruments' six-year elevated capital expenditure cycle for its 300mm wafer fabs will conclude in 2026.
The strategy is already supporting financial performance. In the second quarter of 2026, Texas Instruments reported $5.46 billion in revenues, up 23% year over year, while gross profit increased 30% to $3.35 billion. Gross margin reached 61.4%, up 350 basis points from 57.9% in the year-ago quarter.
Management also credited the benefits of 300mm production as a factor supporting its strong cash generation. The company generated free cash flow of $2.74 billion in the second quarter, up from $1.33 billion in the year-ago quarter. Trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $6.53 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 271% from $1.76 billion in the year-ago period.
Higher factory utilization could provide another margin boost. As much of TXN's manufacturing cost is fixed, stronger production spreads those costs over more chips. Management expects to equip its existing clean-room capacity based on customer demand, allowing it to increase output without immediately taking on the full cost of building new facilities.
TXN is entering this phase with lower capital spending requirements. The company expects 2026 capital expenditures of $2-$3 billion, down from $4.55 billion in 2025.
As 300mm capacity ramps up and utilization rises, TXN could benefit from lower unit costs, better operating leverage and stronger free cash flow. However, the pace of margin expansion will depend on demand and how quickly the new facilities reach efficient utilization.
What TXN's Rivals Are Doing to Improve Manufacturing Margins
Texas Instruments' major competitors, Analog Devices, Inc. ADI and ON Semiconductor Corporation ON, have different strategies to improve manufacturing margins.
Analog Devices is enhancing its manufacturing margins by executing a multi-pronged strategy centered around a hybrid manufacturing model, strategic price increases and optimized asset utilization. With the hybrid manufacturing model, ADI can swiftly pivot production based on demand without incurring heavy capital expenditures. The strategy helps the company protect margins from the fixed-cost burdens of overbuilding factories and supports high free cash flow conversion.
In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Analog Devices' revenues increased 40% year-over-year to $4.02 billion, while non-GAAP gross profit jumped 46% to $2.92 billion. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 72.5%, up 330 basis points from 69.2% in the year-ago quarter. Its trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $4.94 billion in the third quarter, up 34% from $3.68 billion in the year-ago period.
ON Semiconductor is taking a more direct approach to manufacturing efficiency through its Fab Right strategy. The company is consolidating its manufacturing footprint and expanding 300mm capacity while exiting less efficient facilities. ON claims that its streamlined fabrication footprint could operate at about 17% lower cost at full utilization.
ON Semiconductor's non-GAAP gross margin improved 80 basis points sequentially to 39.3% in second-quarter 2026, while manufacturing utilization rose to 83% from 77%. Management expects sequential gross margin expansion through 2026 and guided third-quarter non-GAAP gross margin to 40%-42% on revenues of $1.65-$1.75 billion. The planned Mountain Top and Philippines facility divestitures are expected to generate about $35 million of annualized savings, with benefits beginning in 2027 and fully realized in 2028. Management forecasts these actions represent roughly 50 basis points of the planned 200 basis points of gross margin improvement from Fab Right initiatives.

Conference call at 3:30 p.m. Central time today on ti.com/ir
DALLAS (July 22, 2026) – Texas Instruments Incorporated (TI) (Nasdaq: TXN) today reported second quarter revenue of $5.46 billion, net income of $1.98 billion and earnings per share of $2.14. Earnings per share included a 5-cent benefit that was not in the company's original guidance.
Regarding the company's performance and returns to shareholders, Haviv Ilan, TI's chairman, president and CEO, made the following comments:
•"Revenue increased 13% sequentially and 23% from the same quarter a year ago with broad growth led by industrial, data center and automotive.
•"Our cash flow from operations of $8.7 billion for the trailing 12 months again underscored the strength of our business model, the quality of our product portfolio and the benefit of 300mm production. Free cash flow for the same period was $6.5 billion.
•"Over the past 12 months we invested $3.9 billion in R&D and SG&A, invested $3.3 billion in capital expenditures and returned $5.8 billion to owners.
•"TI's third quarter outlook is for revenue in the range of $5.65 billion to $6.15 billion and earnings per share between $2.23 and $2.57."
